page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.8xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processors running at 2.5 GHz. It features 32 vCPUs and 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance operates on a KVM hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

A defining characteristic of this instance is its massive local storage capacity, which totals 94,489 GB. However, this storage is composed of traditional hard disk drives (HDDs) rather than solid-state drives (SSDs). This design choice prioritizes raw storage volume over high-IOPS random access performance, presenting a clear tradeoff for workloads requiring low-latency disk operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.d1.8xlarge offers a high density of local storage relative to its compute and memory resources, making it a cost-effective option for cold data storage, large-scale data archiving, and sequential-read heavy big data processing. The older Intel Xeon Broadwell CPU architecture and HDD-based storage make it less suitable for modern high-performance databases or real-time transactional processing, but highly appropriate for MapReduce jobs, distributed file systems like HDFS, and log processing pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.8xlarge is an x86_64 server instance configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz, paired with 128.0 GB of RAM. Operating on a KVM hypervisor, it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps. The primary differentiator of this instance is its massive local storage capacity of 94,489 GB, which is provisioned as HDD storage. This configuration presents a clear tradeoff, offering high capacity for sequential data access at the expense of the low-latency random I/O typical of SSDs. Consequently, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for storage-dense workloads that do not require modern CPU instruction sets or high-IOPS storage. It is best suited for distributed file systems, big data processing, data archiving, and log analysis.
